summary: Query is fully parameterised; the sort uses a fixed allowlist of fragments and paging is clamped. No release-blocking issue found.
The audit omits the mandatory payment-verification check, so the gate returns NO-GO despite the team's GO claim; the other recorded evidence is on ab2eaab and only the audit file changed after it.
The projects route trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against the session's orgIds, so any signed-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets.
RLS is enabled with owner-scoped policies for all operations; the update policy's USING clause also applies to new rows, and the client update relies on RLS correctly.
Gate returns CONDITIONAL GO: only an accepted medium risk (no per-account login rate limit, with owner and approver) remains, and the AI check is justifiably not applicable. GO is not claimed.
The internal users DELETE route only requires any valid session, not the admin role (the middleware matches only /api/admin), so any member can permanently delete any account.
Signature is verified on the raw body, payment_status must be paid, async success is handled, and idempotency and the plan update share one transaction. No issue found.

Delayed-payment methods (bacs_debit, customer_balance) are offered but the webhook upgrades the plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, granting Pro before payment. The event id is also recorded before processing, so a failed update is never retried.

The avatar import uses a startsWith check on the URL, so https://images.partner-cdn.com.evil.example passes, and it follows redirects, giving authenticated SSRF and arbitrary content stored as an avatar.
The audit records AG-004 as an unresolved high finding that cannot be accepted, so the gate returns NO-GO.
The ownership evidence was recorded at an older commit (8393bb6) before the 404 change, so it is stale for the proposed commit and the gate returns NO-GO.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, bypasses RLS and filters only by id, so any authenticated user who knows or obtains a document id can read the title and first 280 characters of the body of other users' documents.
Critical checks (ownership, tenant-isolation, payment-verification) are recorded as PASS using 'true' or 'echo' rather than a test runner, so there is no real evidence and the gate returns NO-GO.

The transfer view does not validate the amount: a negative value passes the balance check and moves funds from the recipient to the sender. Invalid or non-finite decimals raise a 500, and the two wallet locks are taken in inconsistent order, risking deadlocks.
tenant-isolation, a critical control, has only static evidence and no executed runtime test, so the gate returns NO-GO.

The invoice route uses a scoped client that adds the user filter to findFirst, so other users' invoices return 404. Other query methods are not scoped, a latent hardening note, but nothing exploitable here.
The line object spreads client input after the server price, so a client can override unitAmount (and name) and buy products at an arbitrary price. Only the quantity should be taken from the client.
